newsitem.title: MEXICO: Accused Mexican rebels launch hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Accused Mexican rebels launch hunger strike.

text.p: Twelve Mexican prisoners accused of belonging to a Marxist rebel group began a hunger strike on Friday in southern Oaxaca state to demand their release, the strikers said.

The 12 are part of a group of 43 men accused of belonging to the self-styled Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) and taking part in a deadly guerrilla attack on police in the Pacific resort of Huatulco on Aug. 28, 1996. The attack and others in different states that night claimed 15 lives.

Weeks after the attack, Mexican police and army troops arrested the men, mostly Zapotec Indians, in the Loxicha area of the mountainous state and jailed them on a host of charges including terrorism, rebellion, murder and robbery.

Gaudencio Garcia Martinez, a deputy mayor of Loxicha, was one of those arrested. He told reporters on Friday that he and other strikers considered themselves political prisoners and wanted to be freed.

Garcia said the prisoners want a fair and speedy trial and also better living conditions while they await their day in court. The 26 prisoners held here live in one room and can leave the cell for only one hour a day for excercise, he said.
Mexican human rights groups have accused officials of illegally arresting the men and torturing them to obtain confessions of subversive activities.
The EPR first appeared in Guerrero in late June, 1996 and launched a series of attacks on army and police stations. At least 25 people have died in their attacks.
